history.summary: Dedicated to Lord Shiva with a swayambhu (self-manifested) lingam said to have been discovered underground in 1844. Popularly called the Kali Paltan Mandir because it stood near the cantonment where Indian sepoys (the 'Kali Paltan' or black army) were posted; soldiers planned the 1857 uprising here and used the temple well, and a war memorial to the 1857 martyrs stands in the premises. The old complex was demolished in 1944; the present modern structure was built in 1968 with a hexagonal hall, additions in 1987, and a 4.5 kg gold-plated kalash installed in 2001. It also houses a Radha-Krishna shrine and a newer Durga shrine.

town_description: Meerut, in western Uttar Pradesh about 70 km northeast of Delhi, is one of the NCR's largest cities - known as the 'Sports City of India' for its sports-goods industry - and is historically famous as the city where the 1857 uprising began.

travel.airport: Meerut Airport has limited services; the nearest major airport is Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~70-90 km)
travel.railway: Meerut City Junction is the nearest major station (~2-3 km from most city temples); the city has seven railway stations
travel.road: Well connected via NH-58 and the Delhi-Meerut Expressway; city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis available

visitor_information.best_time: October-February (winter); one source suggests March and July - verify
